messages.author: 3a00871147d992ba
messages.subject: image
parts:
hi, guys, I recently learned ggplot2 (version:3.2.1)from a book ,R Graphics Cookbook. I used the data,cabbage_exp, from gcookbook package, to try to put labels on stacked bar graph. When I used all of codes the book provided ,but I get the wrong results. the text label at the wrong place. I did this in macOS and Windows. I got same results.
library(tidyverse)
library(gcookbook)
ce<-cabbage_exp%>%group_by(Date)%>%mutate(label_y=cumsum(Weight))
 ggplot(ce,aes(x=Date,y=Weight,fill=Cultivar))
+ geom_bar(stat="identity")
+ geom_text(aes(y=label_y,label=Weight),vjust=1.5,colour="white")
I think the ggplot2 has some problem ,does anyone can solve it?(top panel is what I did. bottom is the book provided)
Thanks!

messages.author: 3a7a3c0921be5f3e
messages.subject: Re: image
parts:
Hi, 
When you add "position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5)" in the geom_text, you will get the result in the figure.

library(tidyverse)
library(gcookbook)
ce<-cabbage_exp%>%group_by(Date)%>%mutate(label_y=cumsum(Weight))

ggplot(ce,aes(x=Date,y=Weight,fill=Cultivar))
+ geom_bar(stat="identity")
+ geom_text(aes(y=label_y,label=Weight),vjust=1.5,colour="white",position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5))

messages.author: 1e82ea932416652e
messages.subject: Re: image
parts:
Your problem is the order in which C39 and C52 are plotting. In the Cookbook version, c39 is on stacked on the bottom; in your version, c39 is stacked on top. The geom_text() labels are printing in the same (correct) place in both versions.

This is normally corrected by reordering the factor levels. See the forecats package for easy ways to reorder factors.

This is also often a problem when using character data as categorical variables in ggplot2 plots; we often need to convert them to factors and order them for plotting.

- Tom

The good news is that Hadley is starting a new version of the book with up to date references on how to do things.

The bad news is that it is still super early on and there's nothing in there about stacked bar charts.
